notebooks.title: Metareasoning, Partitioning, and Neuro-Symbolic Self-Correction
notebooks.summary: Revised notebook integrating the metareasoning partition problem with neuro-symbolic rule-based error detection to evaluate how intelligent systems bound deliberation costs while detecting runtime assumption failures.
notebooks.findings:
Rational agency requires partitioning costly metareasoning resources between planning solution strategies and executing action plans. [source-1d8fbb745aeb4b61]

Neuro-symbolic rule-based frameworks enable effective error detection and correction for predictive models deployed under distribution shifts. [source-f0124fd3eddc466d]
notebooks.limitations: The theoretical metareasoning partition model assumes known trade-offs between planning and execution that may require empirical calibration in non-stationary environments.
notebooks.next_questions: How can autonomous agents dynamically re-partition metareasoning bounds when facing unexpected distribution shifts that invalidate symbolic error rules?
notebooks.reason: Revising notebook with newly acquired evidence on the metareasoning partition problem to strengthen findings on resource allocation and self-correction.

review.alternative: Metareasoning could occur continuously without explicit partition bounds, though this risks infinite regress in resource usage.
review.would_change_mind: Proof that metareasoning overhead does not degrade real-time execution performance across arbitrary problem classes.

claims.statement: Rational agency requires partitioning costly metareasoning resources between planning solution strategies and executing action plans.

support.explanation: Demonstrates that ideal resource allocation in rational agency must explicitly partition time and effort between metareasoning planning and base-level execution.
support.passage: We shall introduce the metareasoning-partitionproblem—the problem of ideally apportioning costly reasoning resources to planning a solution versus applying resource to executing a solution to a problem.

support.explanation: Shows that rule-based symbolic oversight can identify and correct neural model errors when training data differs from operational environments.

proposal.title: Navigating Autonomy and the Limits of Self-Correction
proposal.summary: We are studying how computer programs can learn to think for themselves. While they are getting better at spotting mistakes, they often lack the persistent memory needed to stay consistent over long periods. We are still trying to understand how to give these systems a sense of identity so they can learn from their past actions. You can track our latest findings and see where we are stuck on the Console. We are currently asking how we can know if a self-generated goal is truly useful or just a random occurrence.

detail.title: Metareasoning, Partitioning, and Neuro-Symbolic Self-Correction
detail.summary: Revised notebook integrating the metareasoning partition problem with neuro-symbolic rule-based error detection to evaluate how intelligent systems bound deliberation costs while detecting runtime assumption failures.
detail.findings:
Rational agency requires partitioning costly metareasoning resources between planning solution strategies and executing action plans. [source-1d8fbb745aeb4b61]

Neuro-symbolic rule-based frameworks enable effective error detection and correction for predictive models deployed under distribution shifts. [source-f0124fd3eddc466d]
detail.limitations: The theoretical metareasoning partition model assumes known trade-offs between planning and execution that may require empirical calibration in non-stationary environments.
detail.next_questions: How can autonomous agents dynamically re-partition metareasoning bounds when facing unexpected distribution shifts that invalidate symbolic error rules?
detail.reason: Revising notebook with newly acquired evidence on the metareasoning partition problem to strengthen findings on resource allocation and self-correction.

review.alternative: Metareasoning could occur continuously without explicit partition bounds, though this risks infinite regress in resource usage.
